subject: Biology
source: Edexcel (Pearson) GCSE (9-1) Biology 1BI0 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered topics 1–5 (Key concepts; Cells and control; Genetics; Natural selection and genetic modification; Health, disease and development of medicines).

specPoints.specTitle: Animal and plant cell structure: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, cell membrane, cytoplasm, cell wall, vacuole, chloroplasts; function of each
Eukaryotic vs prokaryotic cells; bacterial cell structure including plasmids and absence of a true nucleus
Specialised cells: sperm, egg, ciliated, root hair; how structure relates to function
Microscopy: light vs electron microscopes; magnification calculations; using SI units (mm, μm, nm)
Enzymes as biological catalysts: lock-and-key model; effect of temperature, pH, substrate concentration on rate (calculation of rate)
Diffusion, osmosis and active transport; calculations of percentage change in mass (osmosis required practical)
Mitosis: stages of the cell cycle; growth and asexual reproduction
Cell differentiation and stem cells: embryonic and adult; ethical issues; meristems in plants
The nervous system: structure of neurones (sensory, relay, motor); reflex arc; synapses (HT only — chemical transmission detail)
The brain: cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla; investigation of brain function by case studies and scanning techniques
The eye: structure and function of cornea, iris, lens, retina, optic nerve; common defects (long-sightedness, short-sightedness, cataracts, colour-blindness)
Sexual and asexual reproduction: meiosis vs mitosis; advantages and disadvantages of each
DNA: structure as a double helix of nucleotides; the genome; genes and proteins; genetic code (codon → amino acid) (HT only — protein synthesis from mRNA)
Genetic inheritance: genotype, phenotype, alleles, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous; Punnett squares for monohybrid crosses
Inherited disorders: cystic fibrosis (recessive), polydactyly (dominant); ethical implications of genetic testing
Variation: genetic and environmental causes; mutations and continuous vs discontinuous variation
Evolution by natural selection: Darwin's theory; evidence including fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria
Classification: Linnaean system (kingdom → species); the three-domain system; binomial nomenclature
Selective breeding and genetic engineering: examples (high-yield crops, disease resistance); ethical concerns
Genetic modification techniques (HT only — describe steps including restriction enzymes and ligase, plasmid vectors)
Health and disease: definitions; communicable vs non-communicable; risk factors and lifestyle effects
Pathogens: bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists; named diseases (TB, cholera, malaria, HIV, chalara ash dieback)
Body's defences: physical and chemical barriers; immune response by white blood cells; phagocytosis and antibody production
Vaccination, antibiotics and antiviral drugs; herd immunity; the development of antibiotic resistance
Drug development: stages of preclinical and clinical testing; placebo and double-blind trials
Monoclonal antibodies (HT only — production from hybridoma cells; uses in pregnancy testing, diagnosis and treatment)
Core Practical: Investigate biological specimens using microscopes including magnification calculations and labelled scientific drawings
Core Practical: Investigate the effect of pH on enzyme activity (e.g. amylase) using iodine indicator
Core Practical: Investigate osmosis in plant tissue using a range of sucrose or salt solutions
Core Practical: Investigate the effect of antiseptics or antibiotics on bacterial growth using aseptic technique
